thread:
Sam: Heads-up — proposal for config override granularity + telemetry gating. thinking: allow per-route + per-customer overrides, TTLed by default, and wire a dry-run/preview flag in console. want minimal schema bump and safe migration path. putting rough sketch here so we can iterate.

Rajiv: +1 on per-route overrides. quick q: how do you want to handle precedence? route > customer > global? or customer scoped to route?

Sam: Route > customer > global makes most sense for our use cases. but need to support a hierarchal key so we can evaluate in one pass. also we should have an explicit "source" field on the config for audit purposes.

Mei: Agree on precedence. For telemetry gating: do we only emit telemetry if override is active for >X% of traffic or after a successful dry-run window? we don't want to flood metrics with transient experiments.

Sam: Exactly. Proposal: a 24hr dry-run window where override is only visible in the console and not used for routing by default. If owner marks it "activate" or it passes autoSLO (error rate < 0.1% and latency delta < 15ms) then it flips. Telemetry emitted in dry-run as a sampled internal event (low cardinality) and full telemetry after activation.

Ben: Migration question: our config store is currently a flat key/value blob. this needs a versioned schema. We should add a schema version (v2) and keep the old blobs readable for 30 days, with a background job that backfills/normalizes. any objections?

Rajiv: No objections. We should use optimistic migration: new writes go to v2 only. reads detect version and transform in-memory. background job can compact. Also need an API contract for PATCH semantics to avoid stomping. use `If-Match` or `expected_version` param.

Sam: Agree on `expected_version` on the API and store ETags for UI lock. Example config v2 shape: 

```json
{
  "version": "v2",
  "key": "route.quota_override",
  "scope": { "route_id": "r_123", "customer_id": "c_456" },
  "value": { "max_qps": 200 },
  "meta": { "source": "console", "creator": "Sam", "ttl": 86400 },
  "preview": true
}
```

Mei: That looks good. Two small asks: 1) add `reason` field to meta so we capture intent, 2) if `preview:true` we should tag the telemetry event with `preview=true` and not include it in public-facing cost metrics (cost calc job should respect that).

Ben: +1 for `reason`. also for the TTL behavior — what happens on expiry? Do we auto-delete or set to expired and retain for audit? We probably want a tombstone so UI shows it expired and allows quick restore.

Sam: Tombstone approach sounds right. TTL expiry -> mark `state: expired` and keep object for 90 days, with an option to restore or permanently delete. That avoids surprise silent rollbacks.

ConsoleBot: deploy-buddy: config-api v2 patch deployed to staging at 2024-06-14T10:23Z :rocket:

Rajiv: Nice. For rollout UX: propose adding a "preview in orgs" toggle where we can target a percent of customers or a cohort (by account tag), and console shows expected impacted routes and example traces. keeps it safe.

Sam: Implementation plan (short):
- API: add v2 schema + expected_version check (Rajiv)
- Store: add tombstones + TTL background job (Ben)
- Console: preview UI + percent targeting + dry-run timeline (Mei)
- Telemetry: preview-tagged events + gating rules + exclusion from cost reports (Sam)
- Migration: read-path transforms + background compaction (Ben/Rajiv)

Mei: Can we add a telemetry gating flag `telemetry_level: [none, sample, full]`? default `sample` in preview, `full` on activation. gives us flexibility.

Sam: Yes — add `telemetry_level` to `meta`. default behavior: preview -> `sample`, manual activate -> `full`, auto-activate -> `full`.

Ben: I'll spike the TTL/tombstone job this week. Rajiv can you spec the API changes and the `expected_version` flow?

Rajiv: Yup — will drop a short API PR and an OpenAPI snippet tomorrow.

Sam: Cool. action items captured. If nobody objects, I'll file a small RFC and link the API PR + console mocks. plan to pilot on dedicated routing quotas first. :thumbsup:

Mei: Sounds good. One more note — let's make sure the cost calc job runs with a `hide_preview` flag so finance doesn't see preview traffic in daily billing spikes. I'll loop in finance briefly.

Ben: +1. Thanks all.
